cards.title: Speed score on phones
cards.note: Google Lighthouse’s performance score, out of 100.

cards.title: Time until the page’s main content shows
cards.note: Google counts 2.5 seconds or less as good. Pages under that line: 5 of 7 on the current site, 4 of 7 on the new one.

cards.title: Data downloaded per page
cards.note: The new pages are about an eighth of the size of the current ones. A small page matters most on a weak signal.

cards.title: Files requested per page
cards.note: Each file is another trip to a server before the page is complete.

cards.title: Search engine score
cards.note: Lighthouse SEO, out of 100, the new site measured with its launch switch on. 100 on 7 of 7 new pages.

cards.title: Accessibility score
cards.note: Lighthouse accessibility, out of 100: how well a page works with a screen reader, a keyboard or large text.

cards.title: Accessibility problems found
cards.note: Page elements failing WCAG 2.2 A and AA, the accessibility standard, on a computer screen. On a phone: 42 on the current site, 0 on the new one.

ai.today: An AI assistant with web search, asked about the nursery by name three times, gave on average 22 of 46 facts. Without search, three assistants knew on average 0.4 of 46. (The name is not counted: the question gives it.) Search cannot reach the new site until it is live, so this test is repeated after launch.

cards.title: An AI model given each page
cards.note: An AI model given only a page’s text, asked the questions each fact answers, three runs, averaged.

cards.title: From the words on the page
cards.note: What a program reads from a page’s text without running any script, the way many crawlers do.

cards.title: From business details for search engines
cards.note: Structured data (JSON-LD), the details written for programs rather than people.

cards.title: From the summary files for AI tools
cards.note: An llms.txt file, a plain summary of the site for AI tools, and a plain-text copy of each page beside it.

ai.hoursGap: Of the facts the new pages do not state in their text, 14 of 24 are your opening hours, which the new site leaves out until you confirm them (see “What the new site does differently”). The other 10 are named page by page in the measurement listed under “How it was measured”.
